name: ghex
why: A GNOME hex editor is a classic binary-exploration tool, though a fairly ordinary one.

brief.what_it_is: GHex is a simple hex editor for the GNOME desktop. It loads data from any file and lets you view and edit it either as hex or as ASCII. The project's wiki page describes it as useful for debugging object code or encodings, and notes it is also used to edit saved games, for example to add score or lives. The launcher executable is ghex.
brief.why_it_exists: The wiki frames it as a general-purpose tool for inspecting and changing binary data on the GNOME desktop, for debugging object code and encodings. It also mentions use by people who edit saved game files to cheat.

commands_seen.context: From the wiki's Git Repository section, the command to download the source code from the GNOME GitLab.

brief.install_notes: The wiki says GHex is available from distribution package managers, citing Ubuntu and Debian package pages. Source tarballs are at download.gnome.org/sources/ghex. No accounts, runtimes, or first-run configuration were mentioned on the pages I read.
brief.standout: It is a small, conventional GNOME desktop app rather than a novel tool. The most distinctive thing in the notes is the wiki's own aside that kids use it to cheat at games, which is a more memorable use than the official debugging framing.
brief.status: unknown. The old wiki page says it has been retired and points to handbook.gnome.org and gitlab.gnome.org. The GitLab page shows a creation date of May 23, 2018 but no last release or last commit date. The wiki page's 2024-10-23 timestamp is an edit date for the wiki page, not evidence of project activity.
brief.caveats: The homepage is a retired GNOME wiki archive, so the wiki text may be out of date. The GitLab page I reached had almost no content beyond a one-line description and the GPL license, so I could not confirm current features, supported platforms, or release cadence. Brew's caveats field was empty.
quotes: GHex allows the user to load data from any file, view and edit it in either hex or ASCII.
Useful for debugging problems with object code or encodings.
Also used by kids who cheat at computer games, by adding score or lives to saved games.
fetch_log: https://wiki.gnome.org/Apps/Ghex: worked. Returned a retired-site notice and the old GHex wiki text.
https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/ghex: worked, but returned only the project description, license, and creation date. No README body or release/commit info was visible.
